findings.title: Apply the website visibility restriction to website_name
findings.body: Unlike `website`, `website_name` is not covered by `untrusted_attributes`, so it bypasses `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. For a TL0 user viewed anonymously, the serializer now exposes the hidden website's host and potentially its path, and the updated template displays that information even though `website` is omitted. The `include_website_name` method is also not a recognized inclusion predicate because it lacks the trailing `?`; correcting that alone would still leave the trust restriction bypassed. Apply the same visibility guard used for `website`.

findings.title: Keep website_name synchronized when the website changes
findings.body: The label now uses a value fetched from the server rather than a computed property dependent on `model.website`. When the loaded user model's website is edited and saved, `User.save()` only copies `bio_excerpt` from the response and never refreshes `website_name`. Consequently, the existing profile header can display the old host/path while its link points to the new website, or continue hiding the website if it was initially empty. Update the derived value after saving or retain a client-side computation that follows website changes.

findings.title: Do not identify shared domains by removing the first DNS label
findings.body: Comparing everything after the first label treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as the same domain. For example, an instance at `example.co.uk` and a website at `https://other.co.uk/user` both have three labels and both reduce to `co.uk`, so this branch incorrectly displays the full path for an unrelated website. Use a registrable-domain-aware comparison, or restrict matching to explicitly supported host relationships, rather than assuming the first label is always a subdomain.
